purpose: Close arbitrary-carrier E879 left bijectivity and record a finite-block obstruction for the remaining E1075/E1278 questions.

model.extension: x*none=none; none*(some y)=some(f(y)); ordinary products retain oldOperation
model.verification: The old law is a coordinate polynomial identity. New cases reduce to f(f(b,S(x)))=(b,x).
model.proofStatus: Proved in Lean without sorry or external certificates.

conditionalResults.statement: For finite I, functions f_i:G→G and permutations p_x of I satisfying f_i(f_(p_x(i))(x))=x are all bijective. G may be infinite.
On G ⊕ I with I finite, assume products stay in the block of their right argument. For E1075 or E1278, each row indexed by I restricts to a bijection G→G.
conditionalResults.limitation: Does not settle unrestricted bijectivity: new points could be infinite, products could cross blocks differently, or the old block could already fail bijectivity.

boundedResearch.method: Piecewise affine integer operations with offsets depending separately on signs of x and y
boundedResearch.details: One-colour bases with two or three sign regions; all three-element E464/E1075 bases with two regions; offsets bounded by 3 and a prescribed small collision. These are bounded template exclusions only.

boundedResearch.method: Four new rows over the E1075 integer core 2*x-y
boundedResearch.details: Right-projection new block; old-to-new permutations depend on the sign of x, positive permutation fixed to a four-cycle, all 24 negative permutations; new-to-old maps are piecewise affine with slope ±1 and offsets bounded by 4. The subsequent finite-block theorem excludes this entire construction pattern without coefficient bounds.

boundedResearch.outcome: All GaveUp; no positive or negative mathematical conclusion. An additional E1278 collision run without the term-size cap also gave up with rapidly growing terms.
